facts.statement: Leaellynasaura lived during the Aptian to Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Aptian-Albian

facts.statement: Leaellynasaura was first discovered in Dinosaur Cove, Australia.
facts.quote: It was first discovered in Dinosaur Cove, Australia.

facts.statement: The genus was described in 1989 and named after Leaellyn Rich, the daughter of the discoverers Tom Rich and Patricia Vickers-Rich.
facts.quote: It was described in 1989, and named after Leaellyn Rich, the daughter of the Australian palaeontologist couple Tom Rich and Patricia Vickers-Rich who discovered it.

facts.statement: Leaellynasaura is a small, herbivorous ornithischian dinosaur.
facts.quote: Leaellynasaura (meaning "Leaellyn's lizard") is a genus of small herbivorous ornithischian dinosaurs

facts.statement: Recent estimates suggest Leaellynasaura reached a body length of roughly 180 cm including its tail.
facts.quote: Recent estimates put its body length at roughly 180 cm including the tail.

facts.statement: Herne (2009) argued that Leaellynasaura lacked ossified tendons in its tail, unlike more advanced ornithischians.
facts.quote: Herne (2009) argued that, unlike more advanced ornithischians, Leaellynasaura lacked ossified tendons in its tail.

facts.statement: A 2019 study recovered Leaellynasaura as a member of the clade Elasmaria.
facts.quote: A 2019 study recovered it as a member of Elasmaria.

facts.statement: Leaellynasaura lived in polar Australia, where Victoria was located within the Antarctic Circle during the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Leaellynasaura was an Australian polar dinosaur. At this period in time, Victoria would have been within the Antarctic Circle.

facts.statement: A skull fragment interpreted as belonging to Leaellynasaura shows enlarged eyes and large optic lobes, suggesting an adaptation to low-light conditions.
facts.quote: A skull fragment interpreted as being from Leaellynasaura has been reported as showing enlarged eyes and the suggestion of proportionally large optic lobes, implying an adaptation to low-light conditions.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the large eyes of Leaellynasaura were an adaptation to low-light conditions or simply characteristic of a juvenile individual.
facts.quote: However, the relatively large orbits of this specimen were more recently interpreted as representing characteristically large eyes of a juvenile individual, rather than any low-light adaptation.

facts.statement: Leaellynasaura ate low-growing plants such as horsetails, cycads, and ferns.
facts.quote: Its diet consisted of plants that grew low to the ground, like horsetails, cycads, and ferns.

facts.statement: Unlike more advanced ornithischians, Leaellynasaura lacked ossified tendons in its tail.
facts.quote: A diferencia de los ornistisquios más avanzados, Leaellynasaura carecía de tendones osificados en su cola.

facts.statement: Leaellynasaura's tail was three times longer than the rest of its body length.
facts.quote: La cola era tres veces más larga que el resto de la longitud corporal.

facts.statement: Leaellynasaura had more tail vertebrae than any other ornithischian, except for some hadrosaurs.
facts.quote: También tenía más vértebras caudales que cualquier otro ornitisquio, exceptuando a algunos hadrosaurios.

facts.statement: Although no complete skeletons are known, Leaellynasaura is estimated to have measured up to 3 meters in length.
facts.quote: Aunque no se conocen esqueletos completos de Leaellynasaura, habría medido hasta 3m de largo

facts.statement: Leaellynasaura is characterized by a beak, light body, bipedal posture, four-toed feet (three claws and one vestigial), and long arms and legs.
facts.quote: se caracterizaría por su pico, cuerpo liviano, postura bípeda, patas con cuatro dedos (tres garras y uno vestigial), brazos y piernas largas.

facts.statement: Leaellynasaura had up to five cusps on the buccal and lingual edges of its unworn maxillary tooth crowns.
facts.quote: Leaellynasaura tiene hasta cinco cantos en los bordes bucales y linguales de las coronas de dientes maxilares no gastados.

facts.statement: Leaellynasaura was discovered in Dinosaur Cove, the Eumeralla Formation.
facts.quote: Descubierto en la Ensenada del Dinosaurio, formación Eumeralla

facts.statement: Leaellynasaura lived and thrived further south than any modern reptile could survive.
facts.quote: Esto significa que Leaellynasaura vivía y prosperaba al parecer más al sur de lo que podría cualquier reptil de hoy.

facts.statement: In a 2013 revision, Herne could not confidently assign long-tailed postcranial skeletons or other fossils to Leaellynasaura amicagraphica, leaving only the holotype cranium and a few specific elements.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en una revisión posterior del material fósil atribuido a Leaellynasaura Herne en 2013 no pudo asignar con confianza los esqueletos postcraneales con colas largas o de hecho cualquier otro fósil que no sea el cráneo incompleto holotipo MV'P185991, el maxilar derecho MV'P186352 y el diente maxilar izquierdo MV'P186412, todo desde la misma formación a Leaellynasaura amicagraphica.

facts.statement: Recent studies have not reached a consensus on Leaellynasaura's classification, with some analyses describing it as a non-iguanodontian ornithopod and others as a basal neornithischian.
facts.quote: Estudios recientes no han encontrado un consenso, algunos análisis describen como un ornitópodo no iguanodontiano, mientras que otros describen como un neornitisquio basal.

facts.statement: Leaellynasaura was a small, slender Australian polar dinosaur.
facts.quote: Leaellynasaura era un dinosaurio australiano polar de contextura delgada y de pequeño tamaño.

facts.statement: During the Early Cretaceous, the province of Victoria, Australia, was located within the Antarctic Circle.
facts.quote: Durante el Cretácico Inferior, la provincia de Victoria, Australia habría estado dentro del círculo polar antártico.

facts.statement: The holotype skull fragment shows an enlarged eye socket compared to relatives, suggesting enlarged optic lobes evolved for better vision in darkness.
facts.quote: el fragmento de cráneo holotipo de Leaellynasaura muestra que la fenestra de los ojos estaba más agrandada en comparación con sus parientes, esto sugiere que los lóbulos ópticos se habían agrandado para poder observar mejor en la oscuridad

facts.statement: Leaellynasaura and its contemporaries likely lived in polar conditions with long periods of daylight and darkness.
facts.quote: Leaellynasaura y sus contemporáneos aún habrían estado viviendo en condiciones polares con largos periodos de luz de día y de noche.

facts.statement: The sun may not have risen for several weeks or months during the winter.
facts.quote: es posible que el sol no podría haber salido durante varias semanas o meses en el invierno

facts.statement: The genus Leaellynasaura was named by Rich and Vickers-Rich in 1989.
facts.quote: Rich and Vickers-Rich 1989

facts.statement: Leaellynasaura belongs to the parent group Elasmaria.
facts.quote: Parent group: Elasmaria

facts.statement: Leaellynasaura is classified in the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Leaellynasaura lived from 113.2 to 110.1 million years ago during the Albian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (113.2 to 110.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are four recorded fossil occurrences of Leaellynasaura.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 4
